page: Amazon Web Services r7g.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by custom AWS Graviton3 processors featuring the ARMv8 64-bit architecture and Neoverse-V1 cores operating at 2.6 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU with no simultaneous multithreading. It includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware-assisted AES cryptography. Memory capacity is allocated at 8.0 GB of RAM, offering a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 1 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and no bundled local storage or GPUs, requiring external storage attachments such as EBS.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-threaded capability coupled with low aggregate throughput due to the single-core constraint. In stress-ng and Geekbench, single-core CPU metrics place in the average band (1509.39 and 1433.0 respectively), but matching multi-core figures land in the lowest percentile tier relative to larger instances. Memory read throughput reaches 97.21 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 30.66 GB/sec for uncached blocks, alongside 10.88 GB/sec in uncached writes. Workload-specific measurements reflect limited thread concurrency, recording 1.65 million Redis SET operations per second, 1.85 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and modest performance in Clang compilation (1612.0) and PassMark CPU metrics (772.7).

From an architectural standpoint, r7g.medium delivers high memory density per core, making it a cost-effective option for ARM-compatible tasks that demand reasonable working memory without consuming multiple CPU threads. However, lack of local NVMe storage and constrained single-vCPU execution bound its overall throughput. It is best suited for small in-memory caches, development and test databases, microservices, light background workers, and low-traffic web serving requiring an 8 GB memory buffer.
description: Amazon Web Services r7g.medium is a memory-optimized instance driven by an ARMv8 AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz on the Nitro System. It provides 1 dedicated vCPU (1 physical core) paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The platform contains no integrated local storage or GPUs and supplies a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate balanced single-core execution alongside naturally limited multi-core throughput, reflected in single-thread stress-ng scores of 1509.39 and Redis throughput of 1.65 million SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 30.66 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 10.88 GB/sec for writes. The instance offers a cost-effective memory footprint for lightweight ARM-native workloads, well-matched for small in-memory caches, non-production databases, and single-threaded microservices.
